deltas.description: h>=0 is an exposed necessary restriction for the descent route and arbitrary-comparator energy claim.
deltas.evidence: Take f(t)=t^2/2 on R, beta=1,h=-1,x=1. The printed h<=1/beta holds; T(1)=2 and f(2)-f(1)=3/2 exceeds -(h/2)|grad f(1)|^2=1/2. Take f(t)=t^2/2, alpha=1/2,beta=1,h=-1,x=0,z=1. This f is alpha-strongly convex and beta-smooth. T(0)=0; ||T(0)-1||^2+2h(f(T(0))-f(1))=2 while (1-alpha h)||0-1||^2=3/2. Thus the printed arbitrary-comparator claim fails.

deltas.description: Whole production module, including private step_descent, was reviewed and source coverage is explicit.
deltas.evidence: Reviewed the entire private theorem statement and every proof line, not merely the exported conclusions. It assumes h>=0, beta h<=1 and the global quadratic upper model at the gradient symbol. Evaluating that model at s=x-h grad f(x) gives f(s)-f(x)<=-h||g||^2+(beta/2)h^2||g||^2. Multiplying beta h<=1 by h||g||^2>=0 proves descent. No beta>=0 or C1 premise is required for this purely algebraic implication from the already supplied upper model. In both public consumers C1 guarantees the gradient is the genuine derivative, recovering the intended source calculus setting. The helper is explained explicitly in both lesson proof chains, as an implementation of Lemma3.1 rather than an independently registered theorem.

repairs.proposed_change: Add h>=0 to the printed h<=1/beta condition for the descent and one-step energy assertions. Preserve the pinned source separately. Do not alter the signed-parameter Hilbert-space generalization or claim to repair the singular inverse-power rate.
repairs.reconstructed_statement: For a C2 alpha-convex beta-smooth Euclidean function with beta>0, restrict the step to 0<=h<=1/beta and set T(x)=x-h grad f(x). Then f(T(x))-f(x)<=-(h/2)||grad f(x)||^2. For every comparator z, ||T(x)-z||^2+2h(f(T(x))-f(z))<=(1-alpha h)||x-z||^2. This proposal corrects only the missing nonnegative-step domain in Lemma3.1 and (3.1)/(3.3); it makes no claim about the printed inverse-power rate at singular endpoints.
repairs.justification: The source descent estimate and its general-comparator energy conclusion both fail for negative steps even with a smooth strongly convex quadratic; the proof multiplies inequalities by h or 2h and requires their signs.
repairs.minimality_evidence: Adding only h>=0 preserves the admissible equality case h=0. The beta>0 reciprocal domain is unchanged. No stronger curvature, smoothness or minimizer hypothesis is proposed. Removing this lower bound admits the explicit counterexamples.

counterexample.descent_missing_nonnegative_step: Take f(t)=t^2/2 on R, beta=1,h=-1,x=1. The printed h<=1/beta holds; T(1)=2 and f(2)-f(1)=3/2 exceeds -(h/2)|grad f(1)|^2=1/2.
counterexample.general_comparator_energy_missing_nonneg: Take f(t)=t^2/2, alpha=1/2,beta=1,h=-1,x=0,z=1. This f is alpha-strongly convex and beta-smooth. T(0)=0; ||T(0)-1||^2+2h(f(T(0))-f(1))=2 while (1-alpha h)||0-1||^2=3/2. Thus the printed arbitrary-comparator claim fails.
counterexample.general_comparator_weighted_missing_nonn: Same f,alpha,beta,h, take x0=0,z=1,N=2. q=3/2, g_N=-1/2, S2=5/2. Left side is 5/2 while right side is 9/4. This concerns the general-comparator extension, not a claim that the minimizer weighted inequality itself fails for negative h.
